reactions.evidence_type: human muscle biopsies (correlative receptor binding); genetic mouse model for the reverse direction
reactions.notes: No primary evidence that insulin resistance inhibits IGF1R. In insulin-resistant muscle (T2D, obesity) maximal IGF-I binding to IGF1R is INCREASED and IR/IGF1R hybrid receptors are more abundant (Federici 1996, 1998), the opposite of the stated sign. The causal direction that is supported is the reverse: a dominant-negative IGF1R in muscle forms hybrids, blocks IGF1R and INSR signalling and causes insulin resistance/T2D (Fernández 2001), i.e. IGF1R -| Insulin_resistance. Recommend re-wiring as IGF1R -| Insulin_resistance (or a hybrid-receptor node) or dropping. The current citation (Pérez-Baos 2018) is a review on inflammatory muscle loss and gives no primary data.

reactions.evidence_type: human muscle biopsies (clamp + insulin signalling read-out; receptor binding)
reactions.notes: Insulin-stimulated INSR tyrosine phosphorylation and IRS-1/PI3K signalling are markedly reduced in muscle of obese and T2D subjects (Cusi 2000), and maximal insulin binding to INSR is lower in obese muscle (Federici 1998). The edge is near-tautological (insulin resistance is defined by reduced INSR signalling). Rename the target to 'INSR signalling (insulin binding/tyrosine phosphorylation)', or better invert it to INSR -| Insulin_resistance (muscle-specific INSR knockout, Brüning 1998 PMID 9844629). Current citation is a review.

No primary evidence found that testosterone inhibits the insulin receptor in skeletal muscle. Direction is biologically doubtful: testosterone generally improves muscle insulin sensitivity. Current cite (Perez-Baos 2018) is an inflammation/JAK-STAT muscle-loss review and does not address testosterone->INSR. Keep review; candidate for re-examination or drop.
Smad2/3 are the transcription factors downstream of myostatin/ActRII and drive the adult atrophy program (Sartori 2009).

reactions.tissue: C2C12 myotubes and primary rat skeletal muscle
reactions.notes: Li & Reid 1998: TNF-alpha acting on myotubes activates NF-kB via endogenous reactive oxygen species (catalase blocks activation; H2O2 mimics), i.e. TNF->ROS in skeletal muscle. Modified: evidence is for the ligand TNF (through TNFR) generating ROS rather than the receptor per se.

reactions.evidence_type: genetic loss and gain of function (muscle-specific GLUT4 knockout and overexpression)
reactions.notes: Muscle-specific GLUT4 deletion nearly abolishes basal, insulin- and contraction-stimulated muscle glucose transport (Zisman 2000); muscle GLUT4 overexpression increases glucose transport, glycolysis and glycogen synthesis (Hansen 1995; Tsao 1996). Target should be narrowed to 'intracellular glucose / muscle glucose uptake' (GLUT4 moves glucose into the fibre; it does not raise glucose in general). Current citation (Bhanji 2019) is a cirrhosis-sarcopenia review.

reactions.evidence_type: gain of function (GLUT4 overexpression increases glycolytic flux in isolated muscle)
reactions.notes: Textbook glycolysis; primary muscle support: raising glucose influx via GLUT4 overexpression enhances glycolysis (lactate production) in isolated muscle (Hansen 1995). The current citation (Sarabhai 2019) is a JCI commentary on the glucose-alanine (Cahill) cycle; it does not test glucose to pyruvate flux, so it does not support the edge directly. Keep as a canonical metabolic edge with low evidence weight.

Current citation Sarabhai 2019 (31545302) is a commentary about muscle-derived ALANINE driving hepatic gluconeogenesis (Cahill cycle), not glycogen->glucose, so it does not support this edge. Biological caveat: skeletal muscle lacks glucose-6-phosphatase, so muscle glycogenolysis yields glucose-6-phosphate for glycolysis, not free glucose; the free-glucose output is a hepatic property. Recommend re-scoping or re-citing.

Same issue as MUS-039: Sarabhai 2019 commentary is about alanine-driven gluconeogenesis, not glycogenolysis->glucose. In skeletal muscle glycogenolysis gives glucose-6-phosphate (no G6Pase for free glucose release). Direction OK only in hepatic context; mismatched citation.

reactions.evidence_type: muscle-specific INSR knockout (loss of insulin-stimulated glucose uptake); insulin-stimulated GLUT4 translocation in human muscle
reactions.notes: MIRKO muscle has >95% loss of INSR signalling (Brüning 1998) and no insulin-stimulated 2-deoxyglucose uptake (Wojtaszewski 1999); insulin roughly doubles sarcolemmal GLUT4 in human muscle (Watkins 1997). The effect is on GLUT4 translocation/activity, not SLC2A4 expression; rename target to 'GLUT4 translocation (SLC2A4 at sarcolemma)'. Caveat: MIRKO mice keep normal whole-body glucose tolerance. Current citation is a review (Kim 2019).

No primary paper verified showing VDR activation lowers ROS in skeletal muscle. Closest primary is Ryan 2015 (PMID 26601949): 1,25(OH)2D3 regulates mitochondrial O2 consumption/dynamics in human muscle cells (could bear on ROS) but does not demonstrate ROS reduction. Current cite (Kim 2019) is a NAFLD/sarcopenia review. Keep review.

reactions.notes: Girgis 2013 (24280059): 25OHD and 1,25(OH)2D dose-dependently increase VDR expression in C2C12. Srikuea 2012 (22648952): VDR/CYP27B1 expressed and inducible in C2C12 and regenerating muscle. Salles 2013 (23929734): 1,25(OH)2D3 up-regulates VDR mRNA in myotubes. Current cite (Kim 2019 review) does not document this directly.

reactions.evidence_type: recombinant FGF21 on human myotubes and isolated mouse muscle; muscle-specific genetic models with FGF21 induction
reactions.notes: FGF21 increases basal and insulin-stimulated glucose uptake in human myotubes and potentiates insulin-stimulated transport in mouse EDL WITHOUT changing Akt phosphorylation (Mashili 2011), i.e. it acts on insulin sensitivity, not on INSR itself. Muscle-derived FGF21 protects against diet- and age-induced insulin resistance (Kim 2012; Pereira 2017, the aging context). Rename target to 'insulin sensitivity / insulin-stimulated glucose uptake'. Current citation is a review.

Hepassocin/FGL1 from the liver impairs insulin signalling in C2C12 muscle via EGFR/JNK (Jung 2017). Liver->muscle hepatokine bridge (Schneider axis).

Ricote 1998: PPARgamma ligands repress inflammatory gene expression by antagonizing NF-kB (and AP-1/STAT) activity. Classic mechanism but demonstrated in macrophages, not skeletal muscle; direction/sign correct. Flag: confirm in myocytes.

reactions.tissue: human/rat skeletal muscle and C2C12 myotubes
reactions.notes: Davuluri 2016: in skeletal muscle, ROS/electron leak accompanies oxidative modification of proteins and lipids and mitochondrial dysfunction (reduced complex I, NAD/NADH, ATP). Modified: the ROS<->mitochondrial-damage relationship is bidirectional in this model (mitochondrial dysfunction also generates the ROS).

Kliewer 1997 (9113987): poly/mono-unsaturated fatty acids bind and activate PPARgamma directly at physiological concentrations. Nasri 2017 (28235206): omega-3 supplementation up-regulates PPAR-gamma mRNA in humans (PBMC, not muscle - tissue caveat). Mechanism is PUFA-as-ligand; not muscle-specific. Current cite (de Sire 2018 review) does not show it.

reactions.tissue: muscle cells (Wu) and neural/general cells + mice (St-Pierre)
reactions.notes: Wu 1999: PGC-1 drives mitochondrial biogenesis and respiration in muscle cells. St-Pierre 2006: PGC-1alpha induces ROS-detoxifying enzymes (SOD2, GPx1) and protects against oxidative damage. Together PGC-1alpha preserves mitochondrial integrity (inhibits disintegrity).

reactions.evidence_type: chronic leptin treatment in rats (hindlimb perfusion with insulin-signalling read-outs); leptin activates AMPK in muscle; conflicting cell and mouse data
reactions.notes: Chronic leptin increases insulin-stimulated muscle glucose uptake and normalises IRS-1-associated PI3K activity and GLUT4 in HFD rats (Yaspelkis 1999, 2004); leptin directly activates alpha2-AMPK in muscle (Minokoshi 2002). CONFLICT: acute leptin inhibits insulin action through IRS1 Ser318 phosphorylation in L6 cells and mouse muscle (Hennige 2006). Leptin does not act on INSR itself; rename target to 'insulin sensitivity (IRS1/PI3K)' and flag as context-dependent (chronic vs acute, lean vs hyperleptinaemic). Current citation is a review.

Doyle 2011: TLR4 activation by LPS drives myotube atrophy through p38 MAPK -> atrogin-1/MuRF1 and autophagosome formation; TLR4 KO abolishes LPS proteolysis. The abstract supports TLR4 -> p38 -> catabolism, not NF-kB specifically; route PRRs -> Catabolism.

TRIM63/MuRF1 is a ubiquitin-proteasome E3 ligase (Bodine 2001; Cai 2004), acting on the proteasomal, NOT the autophagic, arm of proteolysis. No primary evidence that MuRF1 induces autophagy. Likely a mis-wired/layout edge conflating the two degradation systems; recommend dropping or re-routing (FOXO3/NF-kB -> autophagy are the real autophagy drivers).
Cai 2004: IKKbeta/NF-kB activation in muscle upregulates the E3 ligase MuRF1 (TRIM63); pharmacologic/genetic inhibition of IKKbeta/NF-kB/MuRF1 reverses atrophy. Direct NF-kB -> MuRF1 link.

reactions.evidence_type: human exercise trials (arterio-venous IL-6 release, muscle biopsies)
reactions.notes: Glucose ingestion during exercise lowers net leg IL-6 release (Febbraio 2003) and plasma IL-6 and muscle IL-6 mRNA after a 3 h run (Nieman 2003). Low muscle glycogen increases contraction-induced IL-6 transcription and release (Steensberg 2001). Valid only in the contraction/exercise context; rename to 'glucose/carbohydrate availability -| contraction-induced muscle IL-6 release'. Note that hyperglycaemia can raise IL-6 in other tissues. Current citation is a review.

reactions.evidence_type: myostatin knockout/antagonist (in vivo) and recombinant myostatin (C2C12); no direct follistatin-AMPK study found
reactions.notes: No primary study of follistatin acting on AMPK was found. Inference has to go through myostatin, which follistatin blocks. In vivo, myostatin loss or a myostatin antagonist INCREASES muscle AMPK expression and activity (Zhang 2011; Shan 2013). That predicts FST -> AMPK, the opposite sign. In C2C12 cells, recombinant myostatin activates AMPK (Chen 2010), which fits the original sign. The evidence is indirect and mixed; it leans toward a sign conflict in vivo. Recommend replacing with FST -| MSTN, MSTN -| AMPK, or dropping. Current citation (Rodríguez 2016) is a browning review.

Castillero 2013 (23866982): dexamethasone induces atrogin-1/MuRF1 in myotubes; dual knockdown prevents dex-induced atrophy. Sandri 2004 (15109499): FOXO induces atrogin-1 (the glucocorticoid/FOXO->atrogin axis). Bodine 2001 (11679633): MuRF1/atrogin-1 are the atrophy ubiquitin ligases (induced by glucocorticoid treatment). Current cite (Ebadi 2019) is a review.

Neinast 2018 (30449684): BCAAs are rapidly oxidized into the TCA cycle, with skeletal muscle the largest oxidation site. MODIFY: only leucine (and part of isoleucine) yields acetyl-CoA; valine and the other isoleucine carbon yield succinyl-CoA. Narrow node to 'leucine->acetyl-CoA' or label as BCAA oxidation into TCA. Current cite (Ebadi 2019 review) general.

reactions.notes: Li & Reid 1998: TNF-alpha rapidly activates NF-kB DNA binding and stimulates IkappaBalpha degradation in differentiated skeletal muscle cells (ROS-dependent). Direct muscle primary replacing the Rodriguez review.

reactions.notes: Wahlin-Larsson 2017 (the current, primary citation): CRP directly decreases phosphorylation of Akt and rpS6 in human myotubes, linking systemic inflammation to impaired muscle protein-synthesis signalling in elderly women. Aging context satisfied.

reactions.notes: Wahlin-Larsson 2017: CRP increases phosphorylation of AMPK and its downstream targets raptor and ACC-beta (cellular energy-stress response) in human myotubes, alongside decreased Akt/rpS6. Direct, aging-relevant.

reactions.tissue: mouse skeletal muscle and C2C12 myotubes
reactions.notes: Bostrom 2012: PGC-1alpha expression in muscle drives FNDC5 expression (cleaved/secreted as irisin). Tiano 2015 corroborates PGC-1alpha upstream of FNDC5 (SMAD3 represses both via promoter binding). Two independent primaries.

Irisin (FNDC5) is pro-myogenic: induces hypertrophy and protein synthesis via IL6/satellite cells (Reza 2017). Evidence is for FNDC5 -> protein synthesis, not a direct FNDC5 -| myostatin edge; rerouted.
Irisin reduces protein degradation and rescues denervation-induced atrophy (Reza 2017). Route FNDC5 -| proteolysis rather than -| MuRF1 specifically.
FNDC5/irisin -| mitochondrial dysfunction: Reza 2017 shows anti-atrophy, not a mito-dysfunction edge; kept map-only.

reactions.evidence_type: BAIBA treatment of palmitate-treated C2C12 myotubes and HFD mice, with AMPK inhibitor and PPARdelta siRNA; 3T3-L1 adipocytes with AMPK siRNA
reactions.notes: BAIBA restores IRS-1/Akt insulin signalling impaired by palmitate in C2C12 myocytes and in skeletal muscle of HFD mice; the effect is abolished by compound C and Ppard siRNA (Jung 2015). It also restores IRS-1/Akt phosphorylation in LPS-treated adipocytes in an AMPK-dependent manner (Jung 2018). BAIBA does not directly activate IRS1; rename to 'BAIBA -> IRS1/Akt insulin signalling (via AMPK-PPARdelta)' or route as BAIBA -> AMPK -> IRS1. Current citation is a review.
METRNL -> TGFB1: not shown in Rao 2014; kept map-only.
Metrnl drives eosinophil IL-4 and alternative (M2, anti-inflammatory) macrophage activation (Rao 2014). Supports an anti-inflammatory METRNL arm; IL-10 is part of that M2 program, shown indirectly.
Metrnl stimulates an eosinophil-dependent increase in IL-4 (Rao 2014).
METRNL -> IL-13: not directly shown; kept map-only.

No primary verified. Note probable SIGN issue: palmitate/saturated-fat and mitochondrial/ER stress generally INDUCE FGF21 in muscle and hepatocytes, so an inhibitory edge is likely sign_conflict rather than supported. Current cite (Rodriguez 2016) is a review. Keep review pending a muscle primary.
Leptin -| myostatin: only a fat-browning review; leptin's muscle effects are context-dependent (see MUS-056). Kept map-only.
Leptin -| MuRF1/TRIM63: only a review; kept map-only.
IL-15 directly lowers skeletal-muscle proteolysis (Busquets 2005) and IL-15 overexpression induces myotube hypertrophy (Quinn 2002). Two independent groups.

reactions.evidence_type: IL-15 treatment of L6 myotubes plus muscle-specific IL-15 overexpressing mice
reactions.notes: Acute IL-15 at interstitial concentrations increases AMPK pathway activation, glucose uptake and mitochondrial oxidative function in L6 myotubes; chronic high IL-15 and muscle IL-15 overexpression also activate AMPK (Nadeau 2018). The effect depends on dose: chronic low IL-15 did not activate AMPK. Only one primary study was found; reverse regulation (AMPK controls IL-15 expression) is also reported. Current citation is a review.

Decorin peptides have anti-myostatin activity (human, El-Aarag 2016); resistance exercise raises decorin and lowers circulating myostatin (human, 2022); decorin also activates Akt via IGF-IR (Suzuki 2013). Decorin antagonises myostatin extracellularly.

Kanzleiter 2014 (24996176): decorin is released from contracting human myotubes, rises with acute resistance exercise in humans and chronic training in mice; decorin is a contraction-regulated myokine. One primary (R=0). Current cite (Lee 2019 review) general.
Decorin -| MuRF1/TRIM63: no direct primary; decorin acts on myostatin (MUS-134); kept map-only.
Decorin -> follistatin: no direct primary; kept map-only.

reactions.evidence_type: recombinant FGF21 on C2C12 myoblasts with PI3K inhibition; isolated mouse muscle
reactions.tissue: skeletal muscle (C2C12; human patient muscle; mouse EDL)
reactions.notes: FGF21 activates mTOR-YY1-PGC1alpha in C2C12 cells, and its effects on ATP and mitochondrial genes require PI3K (abolished by PI3K inhibition) (Ji 2015). CONFLICT: in isolated mouse EDL, FGF21 potentiated insulin-stimulated glucose transport without altering Akt phosphorylation (Mashili 2011). Rename to 'FGF21 -> PI3K/mTOR (myoblast mitochondrial adaptation)'. Muscle evidence for FGF21 activating PI3K/Akt is thin and context-dependent. Current citation is a review.

reactions.evidence_type: genetic mitochondrial myopathy/dysfunction models (Twinkle mutant, muscle Atg7 KO, muscle OPA1 KO, muscle UCP1-Tg), respiratory-chain inhibitors, human patients
reactions.notes: Strong and consistent evidence. Mitochondrial respiratory-chain deficiency induces muscle Fgf21 (Tyynismaa 2010). Mitochondrial dysfunction from autophagy loss induces Fgf21 via ATF4, as do respiratory-chain inhibitors (Kim 2012). OPA1 loss leads to FGF21 secretion that protects against age- and diet-induced insulin resistance (Pereira 2017). Muscle uncoupling in a longevity model induces FGF21 via the integrated stress response (Keipert 2013). Serum FGF21 is raised in human mitochondrial myopathy (Lehtonen 2016). Fix the node label: 'Mitochondrial Desintegrety' should read 'Mitochondrial dysfunction'. Current citation is a review.

reactions.notes: Muscle glycogen synthesis from [1-13C]glucose is the main pathway of glucose disposal and is impaired in T2D (Shulman 1990). G-6-P allosteric activation drives glucose incorporation into muscle glycogen (Bouskila 2007). reactions.notes: Muscle: loss of myophosphorylase (PYGM R50X knock-in) abolishes glycogenolysis and causes massive muscle glycogen accumulation (Nogales-Gadea 2012). Liver: hepatic glycogen falls as net glycogenolysis proceeds during fasting (Rothman 1991). Cirrhotic patients have 3.5-fold lower net hepatic glycogenolysis and 34% lower postprandial glycogen (Petersen 1999). The edge is near-tautological; consider modelling it as PYGM/PYGL -> Glycogenolysis -| Glycogen. The current PMID 32119304 is not in PubMed; no typo variant was relevant (see PMID_REPAIR).
